adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb#remove_member — `group.users.delete(user_id)` mutates the join table immediately outside of `group.save`'s outcome; save failure reports error after mutation already happened, giving false success/failure semantics with no transaction. Confidence 100, P2.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, `group.users.delete(user_id)` will immediately persist the association removal (it issues a DELETE on the join table) independent of `group.save`. The subsequent `if group.save ... else render_json_error` treats `save` as the success/failure signal, but `save` does not wrap/undo the already-applied membership deletion (no transaction here). Therefore, if `group.save` were to fail for any reason (validations/callbacks), the response would report an error even though the member has already been removed, creating inconsistent success/failure semantics introduced by this diff.

User.find_by_username(username) ... end`, which issues one DB lookup per username (an N+1 query pattern). The parameter `usernames` is taken directly from the request and split without any explicit cap/validation in this method, so a large comma-separated list would trigger many queries and group additions in a single request. This is directly verifiable in the diff and could be optimized to a single batched query (e.g., `where(username_lower: ...)`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb#add_members — no `.strip` on split usernames (whitespace after comma silently fails lookup), no dedup, and always returns success_json regardless of how many usernames actually resolved — TODO comment confirms unfinished UX feedback path. adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, `usernames` is taken as a comma-separated string and iterated via `usernames.split(",")`. Each `username` is passed directly to `User.find_by_username(username)` with no `.strip`, so inputs like `"bob, alice"` will attempt to look up `" alice"` and fail silently. The code also does not deduplicate entries and will still return `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, even if zero usernames resolved/added (since non-matching usernames are simply skipped). The finding’s reference to a TODO in this method is not supported by the diff, but the whitespace/silent-failure aspect is verifiably present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members — unclamped/unvalidated `limit`/`offset` params passed directly into ActiveRecord `.limit/.offset`, reachable by any authenticated user who can see the group; resource-exhaustion DoS risk. Confidence 75, P3.

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members, the diff introduces `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`, which are then passed directly into `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no upper bound or sanity checks. This makes the endpoint sensitive to very large `limit` values (and very large `offset` values) supplied by a requester who can access the group, potentially causing heavy DB work and large result sets (resource exhaustion).
